newsitem.title: TAIWAN: BASEBALL-TAIWANESE PLAYER CONSIDERS OFFER FROM DODGERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-TAIWANESE PLAYER CONSIDERS OFFER FROM DODGERS.

text.p: Taiwan baseball star Kuo Lee Chien-fu, a pitcher for Japan's Hanshin Tigers, is reportedly considering an offer from the Los Angeles Dodgers that would make him the first Taiwanese ever to play in the Major League.
Taiwan's state-run Central News Agency quoted Japanese sources as reporting that Kuo Lee was mulling over a one-year, $100,000 offer to play for the Dodgers in 1997.
Los Angeles already have two Asian pitchers -- Japan's Hideo Nomo and South Korea's Chan Ho Park.
Kuo Lee, a 27-year-old right-hander, joined Hanshin Tigers in 1993 after shining as the ace starter for Taiwan's 1992 Olympic team which won a silver medal in Barcelona.
Kuo Lee was 8-9 with 15 saves and a 3.62 ERA in the 1996 season.
